facts.statement: Changchengopterus is a non-pterodactyloid pterosaur found in Qinglong County, Hebei Province, China.
facts.quote: Changchengopterus is a genus of non-pterodactyloid pterosaur from Qinglong County in Hebei Province, China.

facts.statement: The type species Changchengopterus pani was described by Lü Junchang in 2009 from fossils found in the Callovian-aged Tiaojishan Formation.
facts.quote: The fossil specimen, holotype CYGB-0036, of the type and only species, Changchengopterus pani, was found in the Tiaojishan Formation dating from the Callovian and named and described by Lü Junchang in 2009.

facts.statement: The species name pani honors Pan Lijun, who collected and donated the fossil to science.
facts.quote: The specific name honours Pan Lijun, who collected the fossil and donated it to science.

facts.statement: A second adult specimen with lower jaws was described in 2011 from the Paleontological Museum of Liaoning.
facts.quote: In 2011, a second specimen was described, PMOL-AP00010, acquired in 2008 by the Paleontological Museum of Liaoning. It consists of a skeleton with lower jaws, of an adult individual.

facts.statement: In its original description, Changchengopterus was placed in the family Rhamphorhynchidae as a primitive pterosaur related to Dorygnathus.
facts.quote: In his original description, Lü's phylogenetic analysis concluded that Changchengopterus was a primitive pterosaur closely related to the earlier European pterosaur Dorygnathus, and he placed it in Rhamphorhynchidae.

facts.statement: A 2010 study tentatively placed Changchengopterus in the family Wukongopteridae due to noted similarities.
facts.quote: However, a subsequent study by Wang and colleagues (2010) noted some similarities with the wukongopterids, and they tentatively placed it in that family.

facts.statement: A 2013 study found Changchengopterus outside Wukongopteridae but slightly closer to pterodactyloids within the group Monofenestrata.
facts.quote: Andres & Myers (2013) found it to be outside Wukongopteridae and slightly more closely related to the pterodactyloids within the larger group Monofenestrata.

facts.statement: A 2017 analysis recovered Changchengopterus outside the group Monofenestrata.
facts.quote: In 2017, Changchengopterus was recovered outside Monofenestrata.

facts.statement: A 2024 study included Changchengopterus within Pterodactyliformes, suggesting primitive monofenestratans are an evolutionary grade leading to Pterodactyloidea.
facts.quote: A 2024 paper by David Hone and colleagues describing the transitional taxon Skiphosoura included Changchengopterus within Pterodactyliformes and found primitive monofenestratans to represent an evolutionary grade leading towards Pterodactyloidea, rather than a distinct darwinopteran or wukongopterid grouping.

facts.statement: Changchengopterus is classified within the unranked group Monofenestrata.
Changchengopterus is classified within the family Wukongopteridae.
Fossils of Changchengopterus come from the Callovian stage of the Middle Jurassic.

facts.statement: Changchengopterus lived between 168.2 and 152.21 million years ago, spanning the Bathonian to Kimmeridgian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Kimmeridgian (168.2 to 152.21 million years ago)

rejected.quote: The generic name combines the Changcheng, the Great Wall of China, with a Latinised Greek pteron, 'wing'.
